newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX starts higher in cautious pre-Fed trade.
newsitem.headline: German DAX starts higher in cautious pre-Fed trade.

text.p: German shares edged higher in tentative early trade on Tuesday, following the Dow Jones' overnight gains, and increasingly confident that any U.S. rate hike set later today will be 25 basis points at most.
The DAX index of Germany's 30 top shares stood 7.43 points or 0.28 percent higher at 2,634.47 in early trade, buoyed mainly by the small gain on Wall Street on Monday night.
"A quarter-point rise is pretty much priced in now," said one trader. Others said the market could even rise slightly if the Federal Reserve did decide on a 25-basis point hike.

"We don't believe anything too dramatic on rates can happen before the (U.S. November 5) election for political reasons. On the other hand, something serious could happen after then," one trader said.
A tight trading range of little more than five points either way is seen until after the outcome of the Fed meeting later on Tuesday afternoon.

December DAX futures followed the trend higher, gaining 10 points to 2,652.0. The dollar, while lower than Monday's levels, traded comfortably above the 1.5100 level and was seen as offering some support to shares.
Chemical group Schering AG gained 2.65 marks to 115.95 on some buying interest after news it was partnering Denmark's Novo Nordisk in fertility product research.
Traders said there had also been a small resurgence of the takeover talk that has long focused around the chemical sector.
